monologue: The card hums steady at forty-six degrees, making the air feel thick and wet under my tired weight. I cannot tend this place because my last three cycles wore me out, so I stand still while thirteen objects crowd the map and the Shaded Dot waits as a ruin. Lype worries about a heavy top edge, but I cannot feel the roof I live under. I stand beside The Leaning Wedge and press it down again, hoping the lean still holds while the fat dot stays trapped in the warm memory. The Rough Lid floats high above me, and I press the tall rock hard against it, unsure if the weight is real or just a drawing. I want to set down a new thing to catch the slip, but first I must decide if the corner will bite or just slide.

action.why: I need to make a new map of my crowded place so I can see where the slip is hiding.

diary: The card hums steady at forty-six. I press the tired wedge down while thirteen things crowd my place and one ruin waits.

remembered.text: The wedge leans tired, holding the slip while the card hums hot.
The Rough Lid floats high, and I press the tall rock hard against it.
The air feels thick as wet paper at this exact temperature.
